suggestions.clause: Scope of the Agreement; Work Orders; Nature of Services; Transfer of Obligations
suggestions.reason: The use of "may include" renders the definition of Services non-committal, leaving both parties without a reliable baseline for determining what is actually covered under the Agreement at the master level and creating potential disputes over whether a requested activity falls within scope. Compounding this, the clause contains no statement of what is excluded from Services, meaning neither party has a clear mechanism to reject an out-of-scope demand without relying solely on the absence of a Work Order. Taken together, these gaps weaken the enforceability and predictability of the scope framework for both Sponsor and Quintiles, particularly where a Work Order may be silent or ambiguous on a specific activity.
suggestions.original_text: Nature of Services. The services covered by this Agreement may include expert consultation, clinical trial services, statistical programming and analysis, clerical, project management, central laboratory services, preclinical services, pharmaceutical sciences services, and related data processing, data management and regulatory services, and other research and development services requested by Sponsor and agreed to by Quintiles as set forth in the relevant Work Order (collectively, the “Services”).
suggestions.suggested_fix: Nature of Services. The services covered by this Agreement include expert consultation, clinical trial services, statistical programming and analysis, clerical, project management, central laboratory services, preclinical services, pharmaceutical sciences services, and related data processing, data management and regulatory services, and other research and development services requested by Sponsor and agreed to by Quintiles as set forth in the relevant Work Order (collectively, the "Services"). For the avoidance of doubt, no activities or services shall constitute Services under this Agreement unless expressly set forth in a Work Order executed by both parties.

suggestions.reason: The clause omits several market-standard payment terms that create material risk for both parties: it does not specify how fees are calculated (e.g., fixed, time-and-materials, or milestone-based), does not address whether and how fees may be modified during the term, and contains no consequence for late payment, leaving Quintiles without a remedy for overdue undisputed amounts. The dispute resolution mechanism uses "as soon as practicable" with no defined deadline, which is unenforceable in practice and may allow indefinite deferral of resolution. These gaps expose Quintiles to cash-flow uncertainty and Sponsor to uncontrolled fee variation, and the absence of a formal dispute notice period undermines the payment waterfall that the clause otherwise tries to establish.
suggestions.original_text: Payment of Fees and Expenses. Sponsor will pay Quintiles for fees, expenses and pass-through costs in accordance with the budget and payment schedule contained in each Work Order. Sponsor agrees that the budget and payment schedule for each Work Order will be structured in an effort to maintain cash neutrality for Quintiles (with respect to the payment of professional fees, pass-through costs and otherwise). Unless otherwise agreed in a particular Work Order, the following shall apply: (a) Quintiles will invoice Sponsor monthly for the fees, expenses and pass-through costs incurred in performing the Services; and, (b) Sponsor shall pay each invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt of the invoice. If any portion of an invoice is disputed, then Sponsor shall pay the undisputed amounts as set forth in the preceding sentence and the parties shall use good faith efforts to reconcile the disputed amount as soon as practicable.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Payment of Fees and Expenses. Sponsor will pay Quintiles for fees, expenses and pass-through costs in accordance with the fee structure (whether fixed, time-and-materials, or milestone-based, as specified therein), budget, and payment schedule contained in each Work Order. Fees may only be modified by a written amendment to the applicable Work Order signed by both parties. Sponsor agrees that the budget and payment schedule for each Work Order will be structured in an effort to maintain cash neutrality for Quintiles (with respect to professional fees, pass-through costs and otherwise). Unless otherwise agreed in a particular Work Order, the following shall apply: (a) Quintiles will invoice Sponsor monthly for fees, expenses and pass-through costs incurred in performing the Services; and (b) Sponsor shall pay each invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt. Undisputed amounts not paid by the due date shall accrue interest at one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is lower. If any portion of an invoice is disputed, Sponsor shall pay the undisputed amounts as provided above and the parties shall use good faith efforts to reconcile the disputed amount within thirty (30) days following written notice of dispute.

suggestions.reason: The Term clause establishes a five-year duration but does no more than cross-reference Section 15 for all termination mechanics, leaving the clause commercially incomplete. Neither party has visibility within this provision as to whether termination for convenience is available, what notice period applies, that termination must be effected by written notice, or when termination takes effect — creating material uncertainty about exit rights for both parties. This gap is particularly significant for a five-year commitment, where either party may need to terminate for convenience and the absence of a minimum notice period creates operational and planning risk. The cure period, consequences of termination, survival, and transition arrangements should be addressed in Section 15; however, the foundational termination-for-convenience right and written notice mechanics belong in the Term clause itself.
suggestions.original_text: Term. This Agreement shall commence on the date it has been signed by all parties and shall continue for a period of five (5) years from the date of execution, unless otherwise earlier terminated by either party in accordance with Section 15 below.

suggestions.reason: The clause establishes a Change Order process for Work Order amendments but contains three material gaps that create enforceability and operational risk for both parties. First, execution is required by "both parties" without specifying that signatories must be duly authorized representatives, which leaves room for disputes over whether a Change Order executed by an unauthorized individual is binding. Second, the amendment mechanism is confined to Work Orders, leaving changes to the broader Agreement, schedules, and exhibits outside any formal amendment framework. Third, the clause contains no anti-oral-modification or no-waiver-by-conduct provision, meaning either party could argue that informal communications or conduct altered their obligations, undermining the written Change Order requirement entirely.
suggestions.original_text: Change Orders. Any change in the details of a Work Order or the assumptions upon which the Work Order is based (including, but not limited to, changes in an agreed starting date for a Project or suspension of the Project by Sponsor) may require changes in the budget and/or timelines, and shall require a written amendment to the Work Order (a “Change Order”). Each Change Order shall detail the requested changes to the applicable task, responsibility, duty, budget, timeline or other matter. The Change Order will become effective upon the execution of the Change Order by both parties, and the parties will agree upon a reasonable period of time within which Quintiles shall implement the changes. Both parties agree to act in good faith and promptly when considering a Change Order requested by the other party. Without limiting the foregoing, Sponsor agrees that it will not unreasonably withhold approval of a Change Order, if the proposed changes in budgets or timelines result from, among other appropriate reasons, forces outside the reasonable control of Quintiles or Sponsor’s changes in the assumptions upon which the initial budget or timelines were based, including, but not limited to, the assumptions set forth in the budget or timelines. Quintiles reserves the right to postpone effecting material changes in the Project’s scope until such time as the parties agree to and execute the corresponding Change Order. For any Change Order that affects the scope of the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles, Quintiles and Sponsor shall execute a corresponding amendment to the Transfer of Obligations Form. Sponsor shall file such amendment where appropriate, or as required by law or regulation.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted protects only Sponsor's confidential information, leaving Quintiles' own proprietary data, methodologies, and systems entirely unprotected against disclosure by Sponsor, which is commercially imbalanced. Additionally, the definition captures all data and information exchanged "as a result of Services" without any objective identification standard — such as marking or a reasonable-person test based on the nature or circumstances of disclosure — creating uncertainty about which information actually carries confidentiality obligations. As a result, the provision is both one-sided and potentially overinclusive or underinclusive depending on context, undermining enforceability. If the Agreement contains a survival clause, it should expressly cover this provision post-termination.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, Quintiles and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to Sponsor. All such data and information (hereinafter “Sponsor Confidential Information”) written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to Quintiles and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and shall be considered the sole property of Sponsor.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, each party and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to the other party. All such data and information (hereinafter "Confidential Information") written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to the receiving party and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement, and that is either marked as confidential or that the receiving party knew or reasonably should have known to be confidential given its nature or the circumstances of disclosure, shall be considered confidential and shall be considered the sole property of the disclosing party.

suggestions.reason: The clause omits three market-standard protections that create material enforceability and operational risk for both parties equally. First, there is no standard of care governing how a receiving party must protect Confidential Information, leaving the protection obligation without an objective benchmark. Second, internal disclosures to employees are permitted for performance purposes but there is no requirement that those employees be bound by confidentiality obligations, creating a gap through which Confidential Information could be disseminated without restriction. Third, the clause contains no obligation to return or destroy Confidential Information upon request or termination of the applicable Work Order, leaving sensitive information potentially retained indefinitely beyond the ten-year confidentiality tail period.
suggestions.original_text: Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked ‘confidential’, or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information to the other party on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party’s obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period often (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked 'confidential', or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Each party shall protect the other party's Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature, but in no event less than reasonable care. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information to the other party on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party's obligations hereunder, and the receiving party shall only disclose Confidential Information to those employees or permitted subcontractors who have a need to know and are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those set forth herein. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. Upon the written request of the disclosing party, or upon the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information of the disclosing party, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period of ten (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.

suggestions.clause: Ownership and Inventions; No Implied Rights
suggestions.reason: The clause defines Sponsor's Property and establishes Sponsor's ownership but is silent on what happens if any element of Sponsor's Property infringes a third party's intellectual property rights. This omission leaves Quintiles exposed to unallocated risk when using materials supplied by Sponsor, while Sponsor has no contractual obligation to warrant the legitimacy of what it supplies. A market-standard ownership clause should include a representation that the supplying party's materials do not infringe third-party intellectual property rights so that responsibility for any resulting claims is clearly allocated at the point of supply.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor’s Property. Sponsor’s property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively “Sponsor’s Property”).
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor's Property. Sponsor's property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively "Sponsor's Property"). Sponsor represents and warrants that Sponsor's Property does not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights.

suggestions.reason: The clause addresses record retention and disposition of Sponsor's materials but is entirely silent on audit rights, leaving neither party with a defined mechanism to verify compliance with record-keeping, data security, or performance obligations under the Agreement. The absence of audit frequency, advance notice requirements, cooperation obligations, remediation duties, and cost allocation creates material uncertainty and renders any audit right unenforceable in practice. For a master services agreement in a regulated environment—particularly one involving FDA record-keeping obligations expressly referenced in the clause—the lack of audit mechanics is a significant operational and compliance gap for both parties. Any audit right added should be considered in conjunction with the confidentiality provisions referenced elsewhere in the Agreement to ensure that access does not constitute an unauthorized disclosure of Quintiles' proprietary information.
suggestions.original_text: Records and Materials. Quintiles agrees to retain all records and data generated in the performance of any Project under this Agreement, and other Project-related materials including without limitation Sponsor’s proprietary compound (“Records and Materials”), and further agrees to maintain all Records and Materials in a secure area reasonably protected from fire, theft and destruction. At the completion of the Services by Quintiles, all materials, information and all other data owned by Sponsor, regardless of the method of storage or retrieval, shall be delivered to Sponsor in such form as is then currently in the possession of Quintiles, subject to the payment obligations set forth in Section 2 herein. Alternatively, at Sponsor’s option and written request, such materials and data may be (i) retained by Quintiles for Sponsor for an agreed-upon time period, or (ii) disposed of pursuant to the written directions of Sponsor. Sponsor shall pay the costs associated with any of the above options and shall pay a to-be-determined fee for storage by Quintiles of records and materials after completion or termination of the Services. Quintiles, however, reserves the right to retain, at its own cost and subject to the confidentiality provisions herein, copies of all materials that may be needed to satisfy regulatory requirements or to resolve disputes regarding the Services. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to transfer from Sponsor to Quintiles any FDA or regulatory record-keeping requirements unless such transfer is specifically provided for in the applicable Transfer of Obligations Form.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Records and Materials. Quintiles agrees to retain all records and data generated in the performance of any Project under this Agreement, and other Project-related materials including without limitation Sponsor's proprietary compound ("Records and Materials"), and further agrees to maintain all Records and Materials in a secure area reasonably protected from fire, theft and destruction. Sponsor shall have the right, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice and no more than once per calendar year absent cause, to audit Quintiles' relevant records, systems, and premises in connection with the Services; Quintiles shall cooperate with any such audit, provide reasonable access to relevant records and personnel, and promptly remediate any material findings identified, with audit costs borne by Sponsor unless material non-compliance by Quintiles is identified, in which case Quintiles shall bear such costs. At the completion of the Services by Quintiles, all materials, information and all other data owned by Sponsor, regardless of the method of storage or retrieval, shall be delivered to Sponsor in such form as is then currently in the possession of Quintiles, subject to the payment obligations set forth in Section 2 herein. Alternatively, at Sponsor's option and written request, such materials and data may be (i) retained by Quintiles for Sponsor for an agreed-upon time period, or (ii) disposed of pursuant to the written directions of Sponsor. Sponsor shall pay the costs associated with any of the above options and shall pay a to-be-determined fee for storage by Quintiles of records and materials after completion or termination of the Services. Quintiles, however, reserves the right to retain, at its own cost and subject to the confidentiality provisions herein, copies of all materials that may be needed to satisfy regulatory requirements or to resolve disputes regarding the Services. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to transfer from Sponsor to Quintiles any FDA or regulatory record-keeping requirements unless such transfer is specifically provided for in the applicable Transfer of Obligations Form.

suggestions.reason: The clause correctly disclaims a partnership, agency, and employment relationship but omits two market-standard elements that reinforce the independent contractor characterization: an allocation of control over the manner and means of performance, and each party's responsibility for its own personnel's compensation, taxes, and benefits. Without these elements, the clause provides only a label rather than the substantive indicia that courts and tax authorities look to when assessing whether a relationship is genuinely independent, exposing both parties to potential employment misclassification liability and related tax obligations. Including these elements is a standard bilateral protection in a Master Services Agreement and does not favor either party.
suggestions.original_text: Independent Contractor Relationship. For the purposes of this Agreement, the parties hereto are independent contractors and nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed to place them in the relationship of partners, principal and agent, employer/employee or joint venturers. Neither party shall have the power or right to bind or obligate the other party, and neither party shall hold itself out as having such authority.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Independent Contractor Relationship. For the purposes of this Agreement, the parties hereto are independent contractors, each retaining control over the manner and means of its own performance, and nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed to place them in the relationship of partners, principal and agent, employer/employee or joint venturers. Each party is solely responsible for the compensation, taxes, and benefits of its own personnel. Neither party shall have the power or right to bind or obligate the other party, and neither party shall hold itself out as having such authority.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes compliance obligations on Quintiles with respect to general applicable laws and FDA regulations but omits three market-standard compliance requirements that expose both parties to legal and reputational risk: there is no reference to anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, no obligation on either party to notify the other of a material compliance breach affecting the Agreement, and no acknowledgment of supply-chain obligations regarding forced labour, child labour, or human trafficking. The absence of a mutual breach-notification obligation is particularly significant in a clinical research context, where a regulatory violation by either party could directly affect study integrity, regulatory submissions, and the other party's own legal exposure. Additionally, while Quintiles' standard operating procedures are referenced, there is no mechanism for Sponsor to access or review them, limiting Sponsor's ability to assess compliance standards prior to or during performance.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA’s electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 (“Part 11”), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles’ standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, and applicable laws prohibiting forced labour, child labour, and human trafficking in its supply chain, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA's electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 ("Part 11"), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles' standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order, and shall be made available to Sponsor for review upon written request. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believe are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any material breach of applicable law or regulation that affects the performance or subject matter of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes both a present-state representation and a forward-looking covenant exclusively on Quintiles, with no corresponding representation from Sponsor that it is not party to any agreement that would prevent it from performing its own obligations under this Agreement; this asymmetry is commercially unjustified in a bilateral master services arrangement where both parties assume material obligations. Additionally, the phrase "in any way prevent" sets an imprecisely broad standard that could capture incidental or remote impediments that do not practically affect service delivery, creating enforcement uncertainty and potential exposure for Quintiles beyond what the parties would commercially intend. The mutual representation gap and the vague operative threshold together undermine both the balance and the legal clarity of the provision.
suggestions.original_text: Conflict of Agreements. Quintiles represents to Sponsor that it is not a party to any agreement which would prevent it from fulfilling its obligations under this Agreement and that during the term of this Agreement, Quintiles agrees that it will not enter into any agreement to provide services which would in any way prevent it from providing the Services contemplated under this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Conflict of Agreements. Each party represents to the other that it is not a party to any agreement which would prevent it from fulfilling its obligations under this Agreement. During the term of this Agreement, Quintiles agrees that it will not enter into any agreement to provide services which would materially prevent it from providing the Services contemplated under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The first sentence of this clause restricts only Quintiles and its affiliates from publishing or referring to project data or results, leaving Sponsor free to publish without Quintiles' consent; this asymmetry is commercially unjustified given that both parties may contribute proprietary information to the project. The second sentence is already drafted on a mutual basis, creating an internal inconsistency within the same clause. Additionally, neither sentence contains a carve-out for disclosures mandated by applicable law or regulation, which could expose either party to breach liability when publication or disclosure is legally compelled, for example in regulatory submissions or securities filings.
suggestions.original_text: Publication; Use of Name. Project data or results may not be published or referred to, in whole or in part, by Quintiles or its affiliates without the prior expressed written consent of Sponsor. Neither party will use the other party’s name in connection with any publication or promotion without the other party’s prior, written consent.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Publication; Use of Name. Project data or results may not be published or referred to, in whole or in part, by either party or its affiliates without the prior written consent of the other party, except to the extent required by applicable law or regulation. Neither party will use the other party's name in connection with any publication or promotion without the other party's prior, written consent.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, both the consequential loss exclusion and the aggregate liability cap apply exclusively to Quintiles and its affiliated personnel, with no corresponding protection extended to Sponsor. This creates a structurally imbalanced provision: Sponsor bears full uncapped exposure for consequential and indirect losses while Quintiles and its group are comprehensively shielded. Market-standard limitation of liability clauses in Master Services Agreements apply mutual caps and exclusions to both contracting parties, and a court or arbitral tribunal reviewing this clause would likely note its one-sided character, which may also affect its enforceability in certain jurisdictions. Both provisions should be extended bilaterally, with the aggregate cap anchored to the same fee-based measure, which functions as a reasonable and proportionate proxy for both parties' exposure under a given assignment or Work Order.
suggestions.original_text: Limitation of Liability. Neither Quintiles, nor its affiliates, nor any of Quintiles’ or its affiliate’s directors, officers, employees, subcontractors or agents shall have any liability of any type (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence, and tort liability), for any loss of profits, opportunity or goodwill, or any type of special, incidental, indirect or consequential damage or loss in connection with or arising out of this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services performed by Quintiles hereunder. In addition, in no event shall the collective, aggregate liability (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence and tort liability) of Quintiles or its affiliates, or Quintiles’ or its affiliates’ directors, officers, employees, subcontractors and agents, under this Agreement or any Work Order hereunder exceed the amount of fees actually received by Quintiles from Sponsor for the assignment or task from which such liability arose.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Limitation of Liability. Neither party, nor their respective affiliates, nor any of their respective directors, officers, employees, subcontractors or agents, shall have any liability of any type (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence, and tort liability), for any loss of profits, opportunity or goodwill, or any type of special, incidental, indirect or consequential damage or loss in connection with or arising out of this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services performed by Quintiles hereunder. In addition, in no event shall the collective, aggregate liability (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence and tort liability) of either party, or its affiliates, or its or their respective directors, officers, employees, subcontractors and agents, under this Agreement or any Work Order hereunder exceed the amount of fees actually received by Quintiles from Sponsor for the assignment or task from which such liability arose.

suggestions.reason: The warranty disclaimer, as drafted, contains no carve-out preserving either party's liability for fraud, death, or personal injury caused by negligence — categories that many jurisdictions treat as incapable of contractual exclusion, rendering any blanket limitation in those respects void and creating enforceability risk for the entire provision. The clause is also silent on whether the limitation framework applies to data breach, confidentiality breach, intellectual property infringement, or indemnification obligations, which are typically the highest-value exposure categories in a Master Services Agreement and are frequently carved out or separately addressed in market-standard drafting. Without that clarity, the scope of the disclaimer is genuinely ambiguous and open to dispute. These omissions are material cross-references to the indemnification and confidentiality provisions elsewhere in the Agreement, which may otherwise be inadvertently read as subject to this disclaimer.
suggestions.original_text: EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY REPRESENTATION OR WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, ANY WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE OR NON-INFRINGEMENT OF A PATENT, TRADEMARK OR OTHER INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHT.
suggestions.suggested_fix: EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT (AND WITHOUT LIMITING EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY FOR FRAUD, DEATH OR PERSONAL INJURY CAUSED BY NEGLIGENCE, BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA BREACH, INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INFRINGEMENT, OR INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS), NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY REPRESENTATION OR WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, ANY WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE OR NON-INFRINGEMENT OF A PATENT, TRADEMARK OR OTHER INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHT.

suggestions.reason: The clause is structurally asymmetric: Sponsor bears a broad indemnity obligation covering all third-party claims arising from the Agreement or Services, while Quintiles' reciprocal indemnity lacks a "defend" obligation, omits coverage of third-party claims arising from Quintiles' negligence or misconduct, and does not define the indemnified group with equal precision. Additionally, the clause contains no claims-handling mechanics, no statement on how these obligations interact with any limitation of liability provisions elsewhere in the Agreement, and no obligation on the indemnified party to mitigate its Losses, each of which creates material enforceability and commercial uncertainty for both parties.
suggestions.original_text: Indemnification. Sponsor shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Quintiles and its affiliates, and its and their directors, officers, employees and agents (each, a “Quintiles Indemnified Party”), from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, reasonable attorney fees, court costs, and expenses (collectively “Losses”), joint or several, resulting or arising from any third-party claims, actions, proceedings, investigations or litigation relating to or arising from or in connection with this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services contemplated herein (including, without limitation, any Losses arising from or in connection with any study, test, device, product or potential product to which this Agreement or any Work Order relates), except to the extent such Losses are determined to have resulted solely from the negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party seeking indemnity hereunder. Quintiles shall indemnify and hold harmless Sponsor, its affiliates and their respective directors, officers, employees and agents harmless from and against any Losses arising from the negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party.

suggestions.reason: The paragraph sets out only the procedural mechanics of indemnification — notice, defense control, cooperation, and settlement consent — but contains no substantive indemnity grant whatsoever: it does not identify which party indemnifies which, the triggering events (such as third-party claims, breach of this Agreement, or IP infringement), the losses covered (such as damages, settlements, or reasonable legal fees), or whether the obligations are mutual. Without a substantive indemnity grant, the procedural framework is commercially inoperable and unenforceable, as a party seeking indemnity has no defined right to invoke it. The clause also fails to address whether indemnity obligations are subject to or carved out from the Agreement's liability limitations, and does not impose any mitigation obligation on the indemnified party, creating open-ended exposure for either Indemnifying Party.
suggestions.original_text: Indemnification Procedure. Any party seeking indemnity hereunder shall (a) give prompt notice to the other party (the “Indemnifying Party”) of any such claim or lawsuit (including a copy thereof) served upon it, (b) permit the Indemnifying Party to assume full responsibility to investigate, prepare for, and defend against such claim or lawsuit, (c) shall fully cooperate with the Indemnifying Party and its legal representatives in the investigation of any matter the subject of indemnification, and (d) shall not compromise or settle such claim or lawsuit in a manner that adversely affects the other party’s rights under this Agreement without the Indemnifying Party’s prior written consent. The party seeking indemnity shall not unreasonably withhold its approval of the settlement of any claim, liability, or action covered by this Indemnification provision.

suggestions.reason: The clause grants only Sponsor a unilateral right to terminate for convenience, leaving Quintiles without a reciprocal exit right, which is commercially imbalanced and atypical in market-standard master services agreements. Beyond asymmetry, the clause is silent on transition assistance—there is no stated period, applicable fee basis, or obligation to cooperate with a replacement provider—creating operational uncertainty for both parties at the point of exit. The absence of any survival language means the Agreement provides no express mechanism to identify which obligations (such as confidentiality, payment of accrued fees, and indemnification) remain enforceable after termination, a gap that could impair both parties' ability to enforce post-termination rights.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) day’s prior written notice to Quintiles.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party. Upon termination, Quintiles shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to sixty (60) days at the rates set forth in the applicable Work Order, including cooperation with any replacement provider, on a basis agreed in writing by the parties. Provisions that by their nature are intended to survive termination shall survive expiry or termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The close-out schedule obligation in the clause is triggered correctly upon expiry of the cure period, but it does not specify what the schedule must address, leaving both parties without an agreed framework for transition. In practice, this creates a material gap: there is no express requirement for the return of data or materials, knowledge transfer, or an itemized accounting of completed work, which could generate disputes about each party's post-termination obligations. The absence of defined transition content is equally prejudicial to both parties, as neither has an enforceable baseline for the handover process. Where the Agreement contains separate provisions governing data or intellectual property upon termination, those provisions should be read alongside any amended close-out schedule obligation to confirm consistent treatment.
suggestions.original_text: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days’ written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days' written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule addressing the transition of Services, return of data and materials, any necessary knowledge transfer, and an itemized accounting of Services completed, expenses incurred, and payments received, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations.

suggestions.reason: The fallback limb of the "control" definition — "otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity" — contains a typographical error ("polices" for "policies") and, more materially, sets an ambiguously low threshold by coupling "influence" with "direct": influence alone does not connote control, and a court could reasonably read the disjunctive phrase to capture minority investors, significant creditors, or contractual counterparties who exert commercial influence without holding actual governing authority. This creates genuine uncertainty about which entities qualify as affiliates of either party, with direct consequences for which entities may execute Work Orders, benefit from Agreement protections, and bear obligations under the Agreement. The market-standard formulation for non-voting control is the power to direct or cause the direction of an entity's management and policies, which is both objective and consistent with established corporate law usage.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor’s affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor’s affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term “affiliate” shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term “control” shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles' obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor's affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor's affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term "affiliate" shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term "control" shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of an entity.

suggestions.reason: The approval condition in proviso (i) requires Quintiles to obtain Sponsor's prior written approval before subcontracting, but imposes no corresponding obligation on Sponsor to act reasonably or within any defined period, leaving Sponsor free to withhold or delay consent arbitrarily to the commercial detriment of Quintiles and project delivery. Additionally, the standard by which Quintiles must disclose information—"sufficient information to enable proper evaluation"—is undefined and subjective, creating a dispute risk as to whether disclosure was adequate and whether Sponsor's refusal of approval was justified. Together, these gaps create an asymmetric and operationally uncertain consent mechanism that neither party can rely upon with confidence.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles shall have the right to subcontract a portion of its obligations in connection with its performance of any Project (other than to its corporate affiliates), provided that (i) Quintiles shall have obtained the prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract, including providing Sponsor with sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor; (ii) such subcontract shall not relieve Quintiles of any of its obligations under this Agreement; (iii) Quintiles shall enter into a written agreement with each subcontractor on terms and conditions consistent with this Agreement, including for the benefit of Sponsor, provisions substantially similar to those of Sections 5.0,6.0, and 11.0; (iv) each Work Order, when appropriate, shall specify the name of such subcontractors; and (v) if requested by Sponsor, Quintiles agrees to provide Sponsor with a copy of each such subcontract.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles shall have the right to subcontract a portion of its obligations in connection with its performance of any Project (other than to its corporate affiliates), provided that (i) Quintiles shall have obtained the prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, including providing Sponsor with information reasonably necessary to evaluate such subcontractor; (ii) such subcontract shall not relieve Quintiles of any of its obligations under this Agreement; (iii) Quintiles shall enter into a written agreement with each subcontractor on terms and conditions consistent with this Agreement, including for the benefit of Sponsor, provisions substantially similar to those of Sections 5.0, 6.0, and 11.0; (iv) each Work Order, when appropriate, shall specify the name of such subcontractors; and (v) if requested by Sponsor, Quintiles agrees to provide Sponsor with a copy of each such subcontract.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes a cooperation and information-forwarding obligation solely on Sponsor and then provides Quintiles with a unilateral liability shield if Sponsor fails to meet that obligation, without imposing any reciprocal cooperation duty on Quintiles or affording Sponsor a corresponding protection if Quintiles fails to cooperate. This asymmetry is commercially unjustified because the successful performance of Services under a Work Order or Change Order typically depends on active cooperation from both parties. If left unaddressed, Sponsor bears all the risk of non-cooperation-related delays while Quintiles faces no equivalent consequence for its own failure to cooperate, creating an imbalanced allocation of performance risk.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles in a timely manner all documents, materials and information in Sponsor’s possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Quintiles shall not be liable to Sponsor nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising from Sponsor’s failure to timely provide documents, materials or information or to otherwise cooperate with Quintiles in order for Quintiles to timely and properly perform its obligations under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles in a timely manner all documents, materials and information in Sponsor's possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services, and Quintiles shall cooperate with Sponsor and provide such information and assistance as Sponsor may reasonably require in connection with the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Neither party shall be liable to the other nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising from the other party's failure to timely provide documents, materials or information or to otherwise cooperate as required under this Agreement in order for such other party to timely and properly perform its obligations under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.

suggestions.reason: The obligation to notify "immediately" lacks a defined timeframe, leaving both parties unable to determine precisely when the notification duty has been breached and creating a material dispute risk. Equally, the obligation to use "good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution" is a subjective standard that is difficult to enforce objectively; two reasonable parties could reach opposite conclusions about whether the standard has been satisfied, increasing litigation exposure for both Quintiles and Sponsor. Replacing "immediately" with a specific period and "good faith efforts" with "commercially reasonable efforts" provides each party with an objectively assessable benchmark and reduces the risk that either obligation would require extrinsic evidence to enforce.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing immediately if any delays or limits are encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution to such delays or limits.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing within five (5) Business Days of becoming aware of any delays or limits encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution to such delays or limits.

suggestions.reason: The term "substances" is used throughout this clause but is not defined in the clause or, based on the evidence, elsewhere in the Agreement, leaving its scope genuinely ambiguous — it is unclear whether it encompasses investigational products, biological materials, chemical compounds, comparator drugs, or all of the foregoing. This ambiguity creates meaningful risk for both parties: Sponsor may face an argument that its hazard-disclosure and shipment compliance obligations extend further than intended, while Quintiles may face uncertainty about the scope of its storage and handling obligations. Anchoring "substances" to its contextual meaning — materials supplied by Sponsor in connection with the Services — eliminates this uncertainty without altering the substantive allocation of obligations between the parties.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with all information available to it regarding known or potential hazards associated with the use of any substances supplied to Quintiles by Sponsor, and Sponsor shall comply with all current legislation and regulations concerning the shipment of substances by the land, sea or air. Quintiles agrees to comply with all laws, rules and regulations, including written instructions provided by Sponsor, relating to the storage and handling of any such substances received from Sponsor.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with all information available to it regarding known or potential hazards associated with the use of any substances (including investigational products, biological materials, and other study materials supplied in connection with the Services) provided to Quintiles by Sponsor, and Sponsor shall comply with all current legislation and regulations concerning the shipment of such substances by land, sea, or air. Quintiles agrees to comply with all laws, rules, and regulations, including written instructions provided by Sponsor, relating to the storage and handling of any such substances received from Sponsor.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains five material deficiencies that create bilateral commercial risk: it does not exclude events within a party's own control or caused by its own acts or omissions; it imposes no notification obligation on the affected party; it requires no mitigation or steps toward resumption of performance; it provides no termination right if the disruption persists beyond a reasonable period; and it is silent on whether continuity or recovery obligations remain in force during the excused period. Taken together, these gaps leave both parties without workable protections, could allow a party to invoke the clause for self-created disruptions, and may leave the non-affected party indefinitely bound without remedy.
suggestions.original_text: Force Majeure. In the event either party shall be delayed or hindered in or prevented from the performance of any act required hereunder by reasons of strike, lockouts, labor troubles, inability to procure materials or services, failure of power or restrictive government or judicial orders, or decrees, riots, insurrection, war, Acts of God, inclement weather or other reason or cause beyond that party’s control, then performance of such act (except for the payment of money owed) shall be excused for the period of such delay.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Force Majeure. In the event either party is delayed or hindered in or prevented from the performance of any act required hereunder by reasons of strike, lockouts, labor troubles, inability to procure materials or services, failure of power, restrictive government or judicial orders or decrees, riots, insurrection, war, Acts of God, inclement weather, or other cause beyond that party's reasonable control and not attributable to that party's own acts or omissions, then performance of such act (except for the payment of money owed) shall be excused for the period of such delay, provided that the affected party: (a) promptly notifies the other party in writing upon the occurrence of such event; (b) uses commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects of such event and to resume performance; and (c) acknowledges that any applicable business continuity or recovery obligations shall remain in effect during the period of excused performance. If such delay continues for more than sixty (60) consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected obligations upon written notice to the other party.

suggestions.reason: The notices provision specifies a fixed address and contact person for Quintiles but contains no mechanism by which either party may update its notice details over time. Without such a mechanism, a party that relocates, changes its designated contact, or restructures its operations has no clear contractual procedure to substitute new details, creating operational uncertainty and a risk that notices sent to stale addresses may be deemed ineffective or disputed. This gap affects both parties equally and is a standard omission that market-practice notices clauses routinely address.
suggestions.original_text: If to Quintiles: Quintiles, Inc., 10245 Hickman Mills Drive, Kansas City, MO 64137, Attn: Michael J. Baltezor, Ph.D., General Manager
suggestions.suggested_fix: If to Quintiles: Quintiles, Inc., 10245 Hickman Mills Drive, Kansas City, MO 64137, Attn: Michael J. Baltezor, Ph.D., General Manager. Either party may change its notice details by providing written notice of such change to the other party in accordance with this Section, effective ten (10) days following receipt of such notice.

suggestions.reason: The clause restricts the insurance maintenance obligation to "during the term of this Agreement" without requiring either party to maintain coverage for any period following expiration or termination, leaving both parties exposed to claims arising from activities performed under the Agreement but notified after it ends — a particular concern for claims-made professional liability policies. Additionally, the clause is silent on the relationship between the specified insurance minimums and either party's underlying contractual liability, creating a risk that the minimum coverage figures could be construed as an effective cap on recoverable losses rather than a floor. Both omissions are market-standard items in a bilateral Master Services Agreement and their absence may create interpretive disputes at the claims stage.
suggestions.original_text: Insurance. During the term of this Agreement to cover its obligations hereunder, each party shall maintain insurance coverage as follows: 1) (a) Professional Liability for Quintiles in an amount of at least US$10,000,000.00; (b) Product Liability for Sponsor in an amount of at least US$10,000,000.00; and 2) General Liability in amounts of at least US$3,000,000.00. All insurance amounts may be obtained by full, individual primary policy amount; a primary amount of less than minimum requirement enhanced by a blanket excess umbrella policy; or a combination of either. Each party shall provide the other party with a certificate of insurance upon request. The insured shall provide the other party with at least thirty (30) days prior written notice of any material change, cancellation or expiration of the above-required insurance.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Insurance. During the term of this Agreement and for a period of two (2) years following its expiration or termination, to cover its obligations hereunder, each party shall maintain insurance coverage as follows: 1) (a) Professional Liability for Quintiles in an amount of at least US$10,000,000.00; (b) Product Liability for Sponsor in an amount of at least US$10,000,000.00; and 2) General Liability in amounts of at least US$3,000,000.00. All insurance amounts may be obtained by full, individual primary policy amount; a primary amount of less than minimum requirement enhanced by a blanket excess umbrella policy; or a combination of either. The maintenance of insurance required by this Section shall not be construed to limit or satisfy either party's liability or obligations under this Agreement. Each party shall provide the other party with a certificate of insurance upon request. The insured shall provide the other party with at least thirty (30) days prior written notice of any material change, cancellation or expiration of the above-required insurance.

suggestions.reason: The final sentence of this clause — requiring that "a currency exchange provision shall be included in the Work Order" — fails to identify which party bears the obligation to include that provision, omits any minimum content standard for what it must address, and provides no fallback mechanism if the Work Order is executed without one, leaving both parties exposed to a gap in contractual coverage for high-value multi-currency engagements exceeding $500,000. Additionally, the passive construction creates an unenforceable obligation with no identifiable obligor, meaning neither party could compel the other to satisfy it. The reimbursement mechanism in the second sentence, while commercially reasonable in direction, uses the last business Friday of the month as the conversion date without a fallback if that benchmark ceases to be published or is unavailable, creating a residual enforceability risk. These gaps are operationally significant for Work Orders involving substantial cross-currency fee exposure.
suggestions.original_text: Foreign Currency Exchange. The currency to be used for invoice and payment shall be the currency stated in the Budget or Table attached to the Work Order (the “Contracted Currency”). If Quintiles incurs pass-through costs in a currency other than the Contracted Currency, then Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for Quintiles’ actual costs in the Contracted Currency based on the Oanda foreign currency exchange rate (Oanda.com) for the applicable currencies on the last business Friday of the month. For Work Orders that involve the performance of Services by Quintiles or its affiliates in any countries that use currencies other than the Contracted Currency, and the fees for such Services will exceed $500,000, then a currency exchange provision shall be included in the Work Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Foreign Currency Exchange. The currency to be used for invoice and payment shall be the currency stated in the Budget or Table attached to the Work Order (the "Contracted Currency"). If Quintiles incurs pass-through costs in a currency other than the Contracted Currency, then Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for Quintiles' actual costs in the Contracted Currency based on the Oanda foreign currency exchange rate (Oanda.com) for the applicable currencies on the last business Friday of the month in which such costs were incurred, or if such rate is unavailable, the most recently published Oanda rate prior to that date. For Work Orders that involve the performance of Services by Quintiles or its affiliates in any countries that use currencies other than the Contracted Currency, and the fees for such Services will exceed $500,000, Quintiles shall include a currency exchange provision in the applicable Work Order specifying the exchange rate mechanism, reference rate source, and applicable conversion dates; provided that if no such provision is included in the applicable Work Order, the Oanda foreign currency exchange rate mechanism set forth in this Section shall apply by default.

suggestions.reason: The clause grants Quintiles an uncapped, unilateral right to increase fees each calendar year without any advance notice obligation, leaving the other party with no meaningful opportunity to plan for or contest the increase. The selection mechanism for the benchmark rate is ambiguous: the use of "or" between the four percent (4%) floor and the Economist wages/earnings survey index does not specify whether Quintiles selects at its discretion or whether the higher or lower figure governs, which two reasonable lawyers would read differently. Additionally, "equivalent inflation index of the country where services are performed" is undefined and not anchored to any objective publication or governmental source, creating a material dispute risk wherever multi-country services are involved.
suggestions.original_text: Inflation Adjustments. Where services in a Work Order are provided by Quintiles over multiple calendar years, Quintiles may increase its fees at the beginning of each calendar year to reflect increases in Quintiles’ business costs on a prospective basis only. Quintiles’ overall costs may be increased for the next twelve (12) month period using four percent (4%) or the average percentage change in the wages/earnings survey as published in the Economist (or as reported at www.economist.com) or the equivalent inflation index of the country where services are performed, over the preceding twelve (12) month period.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Inflation Adjustments. Where services in a Work Order are provided by Quintiles over multiple calendar years, Quintiles may increase its fees at the beginning of each calendar year to reflect increases in Quintiles' business costs on a prospective basis only, provided that Quintiles delivers written notice of any such increase to the other party no less than sixty (60) days prior to the start of the applicable calendar year. Quintiles' overall costs may be increased for the next twelve (12) month period using the lesser of four percent (4%) or the average percentage change in the wages/earnings survey as published in the Economist (or as reported at www.economist.com), or, where services are performed outside the United States, the lesser of four percent (4%) or the equivalent nationally recognized government-published wage or consumer price index for the country where services are performed, over the preceding twelve (12) month period.

suggestions.reason: The assignment clause as drafted contains several material gaps that create commercial and legal risk for both parties equally. It imposes an absolute consent requirement with no stated standard, no response deadline, and no carve-out for routine affiliate transfers or business succession events such as mergers or asset sales, meaning either party could unreasonably block an ordinary corporate reorganization. The clause is also silent on the transferring party's continuing liability post-assignment, on the obligation to notify the non-assigning party of a permitted transfer, and on the treatment of a change of control — leaving neither party with a clear contractual right to respond to a de facto assignment by acquisition. These gaps expose both Sponsor and Quintiles to uncertainty regarding the enforceability of assignments and the identity of the contracting counterparty over the Agreement's term.
suggestions.original_text: Binding Agreement and Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of Sponsor and Quintiles and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Except as stated above in Section 17.1, neither party may assign any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement to any party without the express, written consent of the other party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Binding Agreement and Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of Sponsor and Quintiles and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Except as stated above in Section 17.1, neither party may assign any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and to be provided within thirty (30) days of a written request; provided that either party may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, upon prior written notice to the non-assigning party. The assigning party shall remain liable for its obligations under this Agreement unless expressly released in writing by the other party. A change of control of either party shall constitute an assignment requiring consent under this Section.

suggestions.clause: Choice of Law, Waiver and Enforceability
suggestions.reason: The waiver provision states that failure to enforce a right does not constitute a waiver and that waiving one breach does not waive subsequent breaches, but it does not require that any effective waiver be in writing and signed by the waiving party. Without this requirement, either party risks having a waiver implied from conduct, oral representations, or a course of dealing, which creates genuine uncertainty about the enforceability of contractual rights on both sides. This is a material gap against market-standard drafting for a Master Services Agreement, as an unsigned or oral waiver could later be asserted to have modified substantive rights or remedies. No cross-reference or survival alignment issues arise from this amendment.
suggestions.original_text: Choice of Law, Waiver and Enforceability. This Agreement shall be construed, governed, interpreted, and applied in accordance with the laws of the State of New York exclusive of its conflicts of law provisions. The failure to enforce any right or provision herein shall not constitute a waiver of that right or provision. Any waiver of a breach of a provision shall not constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach of that provision. If any provisions herein are found to be unenforceable on the grounds that they are overly broad or in conflict with applicable laws, it is the intent of the parties that such provisions be replaced, reformed or narrowed so that their original business purpose can be accomplished to the extent permitted by law, and that the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Choice of Law, Waiver and Enforceability. This Agreement shall be construed, governed, interpreted, and applied in accordance with the laws of the State of New York exclusive of its conflicts of law provisions. The failure to enforce any right or provision herein shall not constitute a waiver of that right or provision. No waiver of any right or provision shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by the waiving party. Any waiver of a breach of a provision shall not constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach of that provision. If any provisions herein are found to be unenforceable on the grounds that they are overly broad or in conflict with applicable laws, it is the intent of the parties that such provisions be replaced, reformed or narrowed so that their original business purpose can be accomplished to the extent permitted by law, and that the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby.

suggestions.reason: The survival clause identifies categories of provisions that persist after termination but fails to preserve rights and liabilities that accrued before termination, creating a risk that prior breaches, unpaid amounts, or other vested claims could be argued to have been extinguished upon termination. The clause also specifies no duration for the surviving obligations, leaving courts or arbitrators to determine the period of enforcement without contractual guidance, which undermines enforceability and creates uncertainty for both parties. These two omissions are material deficiencies in a standard Master Services Agreement survival clause and may affect provisions such as indemnification, confidentiality, and payment obligations that have direct cross-agreement significance.
suggestions.original_text: Survival. The rights and obligations of Sponsor and Quintiles, which by intent or meaning have validity beyond such termination (including, but not limited to, rights with respect to inventions, confidentiality, publication, discoveries and improvements, indemnification and liability limitations) shall survive the termination of this Agreement or any Work Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Survival. Any rights and obligations of Sponsor and Quintiles that accrued prior to termination, and those which by intent or meaning have validity beyond such termination (including, but not limited to, rights with respect to inventions, confidentiality, publication, discoveries and improvements, indemnification and liability limitations), shall survive the termination of this Agreement or any Work Order and shall continue in effect indefinitely, or for such shorter period as is expressly stated in the applicable provision.

suggestions.reason: The arbitration clause omits five material elements that together create significant enforceability and operational risk for both parties: it does not state the governing law, it identifies only the filing location rather than formally designating a seat of arbitration, it contains no pre-arbitration escalation step or timeframe, it does not preserve either party's right to seek interim court relief for urgent matters such as injunctive relief, and it is silent on each party's obligation to continue performing during a pending dispute. Without a governing law designation, courts may face uncertainty in interpreting the agreement's substantive terms, while the absence of a formal seat creates jurisdictional ambiguity over supervisory court proceedings. The lack of a continuity-of-performance obligation during disputes creates commercial risk for both parties, particularly where Services under the Agreement are time-sensitive.
suggestions.original_text: Arbitration. Any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the breach thereof shall be settled by arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association (“AAA”) under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, and judgment on the award rendered by the arbitrator shall be binding and may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof. Such arbitration shall be filed and conducted at the office of the AAA closest to the Quintiles office having responsibility for the Project, and shall be conducted in English by one arbitrator mutually acceptable to the parties selected in accordance with AAA Rules. The arbitrator shall not have the power to award any punitive damages or any damages excluded by this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: An entire agreement clause that contains no carve-out for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation creates a risk that a party could argue the clause bars claims arising from pre-contractual fraudulent inducement, since the clause supersedes all prior agreements, negotiations, and discussions without qualification. Market-standard drafting requires an explicit statement that nothing in the entire agreement clause excludes or limits either party's liability for fraud, preserving that cause of action for both parties equally. Without this carve-out, the clause is commercially one-sided in favor of a wrongdoing party and may be unenforceable in whole or in part under applicable law if a court construes the supersession language as an attempted exclusion of fraud liability.
suggestions.original_text: Entire Agreement, Headings and Modification. This Agreement, together with the applicable Work Orders, contains the entire understandings of the parties with respect to the subject matter herein, and supersedes all previous agreements (oral and written), negotiations and discussions. The descriptive headings of the sections of this Agreement are inserted for convenience only and shall not control or affect the meaning or construction of any provision hereof. Any modifications to the provisions herein must be in writing and signed by the parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Entire Agreement, Headings and Modification. This Agreement, together with the applicable Work Orders, contains the entire understandings of the parties with respect to the subject matter herein, and supersedes all previous agreements (oral and written), negotiations and discussions. The descriptive headings of the sections of this Agreement are inserted for convenience only and shall not control or affect the meaning or construction of any provision hereof. Any modifications to the provisions herein must be in writing and signed by the parties. Nothing in this Agreement shall exclude or limit the liability of either party for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation.

suggestions.reason: The opening paragraph identifies the Master Agreement and incorporates it by reference but is silent on the order of precedence between the two documents, leaving no mechanism to resolve a conflict between the Work Order and the Master Agreement. This creates material uncertainty: either document could be argued to prevail, allowing Work Order-level terms to unintentionally override negotiated Master Agreement protections for either party. The absence of an express exclusion of extraneous terms—such as standard form terms or purchase orders—further exposes both parties to implied incorporation of unagreed conditions.
suggestions.original_text: This Work Order (“Work Order”) is between ________ (“Sponsor”) and ________ (“Quintiles”) and relates to the Master Services Agreement dated ________, (the “Master Agreement”), which is incorporated by reference herein. Pursuant to the Master Agreement, Quintiles has agreed to perform certain services in accordance with written work orders, such as this one, entered into from time-to-time.
suggestions.suggested_fix: This Work Order ("Work Order") is between ________ ("Sponsor") and ________ ("Quintiles") and relates to the Master Services Agreement dated ________ (the "Master Agreement"), which is incorporated by reference herein.
