In the event of any conflict between this Work Order and the Master Agreement, the Master Agreement shall prevail to the extent of such conflict, unless this Work Order expressly states an intention to supersede a specific provision of the Master Agreement. No terms or conditions not expressly set forth in this Work Order or the Master Agreement shall form part of the agreement between the parties. Pursuant to the Master Agreement, Quintiles has agreed to perform certain services in accordance with written work orders, such as this one, entered into from time-to-time.

suggestions.reason: The clause identifies the Work Order and the Master Agreement as the operative documents but does not expressly establish a priority rule between them in the event of conflict, leaving it uncertain which document governs where they diverge. Without an explicit statement that the Master Agreement prevails, a party could argue that the more specific or later-dated Work Order overrides the Master Agreement on any point it touches. Additionally, the clause contains no exclusion of extraneous terms, such as a party's standard terms, purchase orders, or online terms, leaving the door open to unintended incorporation of outside documents that could displace negotiated Master Agreement protections.
suggestions.original_text: Work Order. This document constitutes a “Work Order” under the Master Agreement and this Work Order and the services contemplated herein are subject to the terms and provisions of the Master Agreement.

suggestions.clause: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses
suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains no operative payment mechanics whatsoever — it lists only attachment references, leaving fees, invoicing, payment timing, fee variability, invoice disputes, late-payment consequences, and expense treatment entirely unstated in the body of the Agreement. This creates material enforceability risk for both parties: the Service Provider has no enforceable payment right on the face of the Agreement, and the Customer has no contractual basis on which to dispute an invoice, withhold a contested amount, or challenge an expense charge. Because all substantive commercial payment terms are deferred exclusively to Attachments without any fallback standard in the main body, any gap, ambiguity, or conflict within those Attachments leaves both parties without a contractual safety net.
suggestions.original_text: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6
suggestions.suggested_fix: The following Attachments form part of this Agreement and together govern the commercial terms between the parties: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6. Fees shall be calculated as set forth in Attachment 2 and invoiced in accordance with Attachment 4; where Attachment 4 does not specify a frequency, invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears. All undisputed invoices are due within thirty (30) days of receipt. Either party may dispute an invoice in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt, specifying the basis for dispute; undisputed amounts remain due by the original payment date. Late payments on undisputed amounts accrue interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. Fees are fixed as set out in Attachment 2 and may not be varied except by written amendment signed by both parties. Out-of-pocket expenses are either included within Attachment 2 or, if not so included, require prior written approval from the other party before being incurred.

suggestions.reason: The Term clause defers all termination mechanics entirely to the Master Agreement without incorporating any self-contained provisions for termination grounds, cure periods, notice requirements, written form, effective date of termination, post-termination consequences, or survival of obligations. This creates material operational uncertainty for both parties: neither party can determine from the Work Order alone on what grounds or how it may exit, what notice is required, or what financial and practical obligations follow. The continuation provision governing the scenario where the Master Agreement lapses while the Work Order remains open also fails to address which specific provisions are intended to survive, which could expose either party to unintended ongoing obligations or the loss of critical protections.
suggestions.original_text: Term. The term of this Work Order shall commence on the date of execution and shall continue until the services described in Attachment 1 are completed, unless this Work Order is terminated in accordance with the Master Agreement. If the Master Agreement is terminated or expires, but this Work Order is not terminated or completed, then the terms of the Master Agreement shall continue to apply to this Work Order until the Work Order is either terminated or completed.

suggestions.reason: The clause expressly binds corporate affiliates to all terms and conditions of the Master Agreement and Work Order, but imposes no equivalent obligation on non-affiliate subcontractors and consultants: they are merely listed, with no requirement that they be bound by materially equivalent obligations, including confidentiality, data protection, or security. This gap means that third-party subcontractors performing material portions of the Services could operate outside the contractual framework that governs Quintiles itself, creating meaningful exposure for both parties. Where subcontractors handle sensitive data or Confidential Information, the absence of a downstream binding obligation undermines the protections established elsewhere in the Master Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Affiliates and Subcontractors. Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Work Order. Any such affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of, and be entitled to all rights and protections afforded under, the Master Agreement and this Work Order. Any subcontractors or consultants (other than Quintiles’ affiliates) that will be used by Quintiles in performing the Services are listed below:

suggestions.reason: The clause identifies a list of approved subcontractors and consultants but contains only an unfilled placeholder, leaving three material gaps: it does not establish whether the other party must consent to or be notified of additions or substitutions, it imposes no ongoing responsibility on Quintiles for its subcontractors' acts or omissions, and it provides no mechanism for the other party to object to changes. Without a retained-responsibility provision, Quintiles could disclaim liability for subcontractor failures, while without a consent or notice mechanism, the other party has no practical ability to protect itself against undisclosed substitutions. These omissions create material enforceability and accountability risks for both parties across the term of the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: [Insert names of any subcontractors or consultants, other than Quintiles’ affiliates, that will be used]
suggestions.suggested_fix: [Insert names of approved subcontractors and consultants]. Quintiles shall remain responsible for all acts and omissions of its subcontractors and consultants as if performed by Quintiles directly. Any addition or substitution of a subcontractor or consultant shall require the other party's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted limits its scope to "this Work Order" only, leaving modifications to the broader Agreement, schedules, and other related instruments potentially outside the amendment formality requirement, which creates an enforceability gap and inconsistency across the contract structure. Additionally, the clause is silent on the authority level required to sign an amendment, meaning a purported amendment executed by an unauthorized representative of either party could generate a dispute as to its validity. Both gaps are commercially material in a Master Services Agreement context where multiple Work Orders and schedules may coexist.
suggestions.original_text: Amendments. No modification, amendment, or waiver of this Work Order shall be effective unless in writing and duly executed and delivered by each party to the other.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Amendments. No modification, amendment, or waiver of this Agreement, including any schedules or Work Orders hereunder, shall be effective unless in writing and duly executed and delivered by a duly authorized representative of each party to the other.

suggestions.reason: The Currency Exchange clause contains no operative contractual language whatsoever; it is an unfilled drafting instruction enclosed in brackets, rendering the provision entirely unenforceable and without legal effect. Because the clause is triggered in Work Orders where fees or expenses exceed one million US Dollars in a foreign currency, the absence of any agreed conversion mechanism, reference rate, or rate determination date creates material financial uncertainty for both parties on significant cross-currency transactions. No court could determine the rights or obligations of either party from this text, and the gap could give rise to disputed payment calculations or unresolved currency exposure in every affected Work Order.
suggestions.original_text: Currency Exchange. [Insert currency exchange provision in all Work Orders in which Quintiles will earn fees or incur expenses in excess of one million US. Dollars in a currency differing from the invoice and payment currency]
suggestions.suggested_fix: Currency Exchange. Where Quintiles earns fees or incurs expenses in excess of one million US Dollars (USD 1,000,000) under a Work Order in a currency other than the invoice and payment currency, such amounts shall be converted to the invoice and payment currency at the mid-market exchange rate published by the European Central Bank on the last Business Day of the calendar month in which such fees are earned or expenses are incurred.

suggestions.reason: The Inflation and Cost Adjustment clause consists entirely of an unfilled placeholder and contains no operative text, meaning it creates no enforceable rights or obligations for either party on the commercially significant issue of fee adjustments over time. As drafted, neither party has a defined mechanism, index, cap, notice period, or recourse right, leaving the economic terms of any long-term engagement entirely open to dispute. This omission exposes both parties to uncertainty: the service provider has no contractual basis to pass through cost increases, while the customer has no protection against uncapped or unilateral price changes. The clause must be replaced with a complete, bilaterally balanced operative provision before execution.
suggestions.original_text: Inflation and Cost Adjustment. [Insert cost adjustment provision and inflation provision, if appropriate.]
suggestions.suggested_fix: Inflation and Cost Adjustment. Either party may request an adjustment to the Fees once per calendar year upon no less than sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party. Any such adjustment shall not exceed the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics for the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the date of such notice. If the parties fail to agree on an adjusted Fee schedule within thirty (30) days following such notice, either party may terminate the affected Order Form upon no less than thirty (30) days' written notice, without liability to the other party solely by reason of such termination.
